 ROUNDTABLE: Rutgers vs. No. 24 Northwestern predictions
 Back home after a gritty, season-defining win on the road.
 by Inside NU Archives Oct 23, 2026, 8:00 PM UTC Facebook 
 Link 
 A red-hot Northwestern squad (5-1, 2-1 B1G) returns to Ryan Field after gutting out an ugly three-point victory over former head coach Pat Fitzgerald and Michigan State, and a red-hot Inside NU prediction cohort (credit to Jackson Pick last week for the spot-on call) is ready to talk about where this team is headed.
 Bowl season? Just one win away.
 College Football Playoff? Well, if we copy-pasted this season in 2027, the ‘Cats are firmly in that field.
 But this weekend, its Rutgers (2-4, 1-2 B1G) coming to Chi-city: a struggling team in the same tier as a Michigan State. Last week, NU didn’t operate at its best, but this week, the coaching staff and ‘Cats faithful agree on one thing: they’d like to see cleaner football.
 INU staff concurs.
 Charlie Jacobs (41-27 Northwestern )
 Last week against Michigan State, Northwestern barely survived. However, this team comes back to Evanston to play in Ryan Field, where it is 2-0, and 4-0 overall at home. Rutgers has two studs in KJ Duff and Antwan Raymond, but the rest of the team isn’t very good, not to mention that Raymond is questionable to for Saturday morning. Northwestern will need to keep up with Rutgers in the score column, but if the secondary gets healthier, then it shouldn’t be a problem to stop them a few times. Force a couple turnovers and this game is won.
 Jackson Pick (35-17 Northwestern )
 After escaping with an ugly last-second win over Michigan State, Northwestern should be more than aware of the threat that any Big Ten team can pose on any given Saturday. Though the team traveling to Evanston this weekend is 2-4 Rutgers, the Scarlet Knights have played serviceable football since their Week 1 loss to UMass, keeping it close with then-No. 12 USC and collecting a conference win over Maryland. Still, it’s going to be tough for Rutgers to get past a team on high alert, especially with the Wildcat Wall back in full effect. The visitors’ last-in-the-Big Ten rush defense, allowing 185.2 yards per game, presents a tasty meal for a Wildcat ground attack hungry for a bounce-back game after a so-so 134 yard day in East Lansing. I’ll take the ‘Cats to cruise to bowl eligibility behind a big day from Caleb Komolafe.
 Whitley Williams (42-14 Northwestern )
 Coming off a thrilling win in East Lansing last weekend, Northwestern seeks to solidify its standing in the Big Ten title hunt.
 Rutgers has been the model of inconsistency this season, starting its season with an abysmal loss to perennial FBS basement-dweller UMass before nearly upsetting a highly ranked USC team. It notched its first Big Ten victory last weekend against Maryland and will aim to exploit Northwestern’s vulnerabilities in the secondary.
 Look for the connection between Dylan Lonergan and wide receiver KJ Duff to be a threat. Lonergan has averaged 213.2 passing yards per game this season, but has been extremely turnover prone, recording six in his five games. Running back Antwan Raymond has also been a factor this season, recording 161 total yards from scrimmage against the Trojans.
 Northwestern should stick to its mighty run game. Rutgers has surrendered almost 200 rushing yards per game, ranking 118th nationally per ESPN. Rutgers is outmatched from a talent perspective and the Wildcats will run away with another victory, securing bowl eligibility and proving yet again they’ve emerged as a force in the Big Ten.
 Donovan West (31-17 Northwestern )
 Rutgers started the season in about the worst way possible in a 37-21 loss to UMass, who entered the game on a 16-game losing streak. The internet exploded as it saw a Big Ten team lose to a putrid MAC team, labeling Head Coach Greg Schiano and his group as embarrassments. The Scarlet Knights have since righted the ship a little bit and are coming off of their best win of the season: a 37-30 win at Maryland, but this is yet another game where Northwestern is expected to handle business.
 The ‘Cats will enter the game as more than two touchdown favorites, and this is somewhat of a must-win, given the four game gauntlet that follows. The Wildcats need to reinvigorate their run game and pound the ball into the Scarlet Knights’ chests; they need to prove that last week’s error-riddled performance was a fluke.
 Zac Penson (34-14 Northwestern )
 The Scarlet Knights have had their fair share of struggles, especially after losses to UMass and Boston College to start the season, but they’ve started to come around with a tight game against USC and a win over Maryland in recent weeks. However, No. 24 Northwestern has its sights set on a commanding victory to garner momentum before heading into Eugene on Halloween. As long as the ‘Cats can find a way to fend off Antwan Raymond and KJ Duff, I predict they gain bowl eligibility with a win in Evanston and improve to 6-1 on the season.
 Ben Levy (28-10 Northwestern )
 Northwestern has been strong at home all season, so a return to Ryan Field is a good way for the team to get right after barely winning a game they probably should have won by 10 or more. The one bright light for Rutgers is that it took then-No. 12 USC to the brink in mid-September, but that was at home. Ultimately, Northwestern matches up well with Rutgers and the Wildcats should be able to keep a ranking next to their name and their slim CFP hopes alive.
 Adam Sutro (41-24 Northwestern )
 Unlike a lot of my colleagues, I believe that the 2-4 Scarlet Knights will be able to run up the score a little bit against the Wildcats.
 Northwestern will still be missing critical enforcers in the secondary — most notably Josh Fussell, and likely Robert Fitzgerald, who’s listed as doubtful as of Friday afternoon — while the best part of this Rutgers team is its pass game. The Scarlet Knights rank No. 6 in the Big Ten with 265.8 passing yards per game, due in large part to standout receiver KJ Duff, who ranks second in the Big Ten in receiving yards (741). However, the number that will define the game should be Rutgers’ 25.2% explosive rush rate, which is the worst in all of college football by 4 percentage points. Facing the schematic creativity of Chip Kelly and an NU run game that has already posted 400 rushing yards in a single game this season, the ‘Cats should have another BIG day on the ground and run away with the victory. I expect a high scoring affair, but an end-to-end, double-digit victory for Northwestern.
 Matt Campbell (35-21 Northwestern )
 This one’s going to be business as usual for Northwestern. Last week, the circumstances brought Michigan State a perfect storm of hostility in which it was able to compete. This week, all of that is out the window.
 Just two Big Ten teams playing football. That’s it. And in that realm, Northwestern overwhelms Rutgers in every aspect of the game: the barometers on pass scheme, run blocking, rushing defense and the clutch factor all tip in favor of the Wildcats.
 I don’t see this game being competitive beyond 0-0. The Scarlet Knights won’t suffer as much of a shellacking as Ball State got a few weeks ago, but the one they get will leave a similar looking bruise.
